title: SSFT: Algorithm and Hardware Co-design for Structured Sparse Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models
problem: Sparse fine-tuning (SFT) reduces time and memory requirements compared to dense fine-tuning, but GPU implementation underperforms due to irregular sparse data access patterns that modern GPUs cannot efficiently handle, negating computational benefits.
motivation: LLM fine-tuning is expensive; sparse fine-tuning promises efficiency but GPU execution fails to exploit sparsity benefits.
method: SSFT-Alg introduces predictable sparsity patterns reducing memory access overhead and enhancing regularity. SSFT-Hw accelerator optimizes SSFT-Alg with sparsity-aware design avoiding GPU sparse overhead. Co-design balances algorithm structure and hardware capabilities.
key_novelty: Structured sparsity patterns designed specifically for hardware implementation, enabling efficient acceleration without generic sparse operation overhead.
contributions: SSFT-Alg with predictable sparsity patterns for regularity
Comparable accuracy to dense fine-tuning on BERT, LLaMA 2 7B, and 13B
51.0x throughput vs GPU, 1.32x vs SOTA sparsity-aware accelerators; 19.0x and 1.48x energy improvements

metrics.speedup: 51.0x vs GPU, 1.32x vs SOTA sparsity accelerators

primary_theme: Structured sparse fine-tuning with hardware-algorithm co-design for LLMs
